newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures end mixed, still in range.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures end mixed, still in range.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Friday in a moderate session, with prices still stuck in recent technical ranges amid little reason to move far in either direction, industry sources said.
November slipped 2.4 cents to close at $2.347 per million British thermal units. December settled 1.2 cents higher at $2.532. Others ended mixed.

"I don't see much more downside. I think you 'll see a lot of buying around $2.30," said one East Coast trader, adding evening heating loads this week have kept LDCs in the market and help prop up the cash.
With operators likely to protect storage right into the heating season, most agreed any bouts of cold weather should boost physical and paper prices.
But with temperatures expected to turn more moderate later next week, some saw light pressure ahead.
Technically, traders agreed $2.30 was key support in November, with resistance seen at Wednesday's high of $2.59 and then in the mid-$2.60s.

Cash sources said weekend Gulf Coast prices fell more than a nickel Friday to the low-$2.30s. Midcon pipes were almost a dime lower in the low-teens. New York city gate gas was talked a few cents higher in the high-$2.60s.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip fell 2.8 cents to $2.176. NYMEX said 29,546 Hub contracts traded, down from Thursday's revised tally of 44,655.
NYMEX November Alberta natgas settled two cents lower at $1.05, while deferreds closed down by two to four cents. NYMEX said 174 Alberta contracts traded.
NYMEX November Permian natgas finished unchanged at $2.055, while deferreds again were untraded. NYMEX said 50 Permian lots changed hands compared to 56 on Thursday.
On the KCBT, November settled one cent lower at $2.10, while deferreds ended up by one-half to one cent. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.4 cents to 24.7 cents (NYMEX premium).
